text: Future feature (deferred from 2026-08-16 dark-Stage deliberation on 5D98DBCC): cross-workspace shared read-only serving WITHOUT relaxing workspace containment. The external-path read-sources.yaml design was rejected on NON-NEGOTIABLE Principle III/IV grounds (see docs/decisions/2026-08-16-shared-external-readonly-databases-deliberation.md). Constitution-compliant alternative (Option C): run one graphtor-docs serve process rooted where the shared db legitimately lives and let other dev workspaces consume it as MCP clients. Requires a multiplexing MCP transport (HTTP/SSE or local socket) beyond today's 1:1 STDIO, and structurally eliminates the F6 concurrent-multi-process-file gap. Must carry its own Constitution Check (III + V + authz/exfiltration for the network surface) when planned. Also encompasses truly closing the F6 cross-process read-only ownership/liveness window (deferred from spike 970AE45A). Operator confirmation needed on whether to pursue.

Security hardening (deferred from 2026-08-16 dark-Stage adversarial review of 970AE45A/5D98DBCC): symlink-swap TOCTOU in EngineReadonlyGuard (src/db/store.rs lock:472 / Drop:582). fs::set_permissions follows symlinks and the main db file (index 0) is NOT re-checked with is_reparse_point in lock or Drop (only sidecars index>0 are), relying on the caller's earlier validate_path. Because the guard is held for the DataStore lifetime, an attacker with workspace write access could replace the db file with a symlink to an external target after open; on Drop the guard would chmod that external target. Fix: bind permission capture and restore to the file identity, not a re-resolved path -- a path re-check before set_permissions is itself TOCTOU-vulnerable (the path can be swapped between the is_reparse_point check and the set_permissions call), so do NOT prescribe another path re-check. Prefer an identity-bound, no-follow restoration where the platform supports it: open each guarded entry (the main db at index 0 AND every -wal/-shm/-journal sidecar) once at lock time with no-follow/no-reparse semantics (for example O_NOFOLLOW / FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT) and drive EVERY permission operation on that entry -- original-permission capture, the lock-time read-only application, any acquisition-error rollback, and the Drop-time restore -- through that retained handle (fchmod / SetFileInformationByHandle) so a later symlink swap cannot redirect any chmod; apply this to every guarded entry, prohibit any path-based chmod fallback, and REMOVE the existing per-sidecar is_reparse_point re-check, which is itself the same TOCTOU by this argument; if such a handle cannot be retained for the DataStore lifetime, fail closed rather than restoring via a re-resolved path (verify no regression to the existing exact-permission capture/restore + non-empty-sidecar-preservation tests). Needs its own spike/deliberation as a security-mechanism change (Principle III/IV). Source: Security Reviewer (gemini) P1, corroborated by Correctness Reviewer P3 TOCTOU on clear_stale_readonly_lock.

Security hardening (POST-CAP residual from PR #96 Copilot review, 2026-08-17): write-mode stale-lock-clearing TOCTOU in clear_stale_readonly_lock (src/db/store.rs:649). SAME check/use race as the EngineReadonlyGuard::lock/Drop symlink-swap TOCTOU tracked in 5905CDEE, but on a DIFFERENT, currently-uncovered code path. In clear_stale_readonly_lock the per-sidecar loop no-follow-checks each candidate with is_reparse_point(&candidate) (symlink_metadata, ~store.rs:665) and THEN, on separate later lines, performs PATH-BASED operations that follow the link: candidate.exists() (~:677), fs::metadata(&candidate) (~:680), and set_readonly(&candidate, false) -> fs::set_permissions(path, ...) (~:685). An attacker with workspace write access can swap a sidecar for a symlink/junction to an external target BETWEEN the is_reparse_point check and the set_permissions call; the write-mode open path would then clear the read-only bit on that external target, and the subsequent write-mode open could proceed against the linked file. 5905CDEE's remedy is scoped ONLY to EngineReadonlyGuard::lock/Drop (main db index 0 + sidecar capture/restore), so this write-mode clearing path in clear_stale_readonly_lock remains unaddressed. REMEDY (identity-bound, no-follow -- do NOT prescribe another path re-check, which is itself TOCTOU-vulnerable because the path can be swapped between the re-check and set_permissions): open each sidecar candidate once with no-follow/no-reparse semantics (O_NOFOLLOW on Unix; FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT / no-follow open on Windows) and drive EVERY permission operation -- the read-only probe AND the read-only clear -- through that retained handle (fchmod / SetFileInformationByHandle); prohibit any path-based chmod fallback; if a no-follow handle cannot be obtained, FAIL CLOSED (refuse the write-mode open) rather than mutating via a re-resolved path. Preserve the existing regression tests (e.g. open_sqlite_refuses_a_dangling_symlinked_wal_sidecar and the refuse-linked-sidecar cases). RELATIONSHIP: this is the same-mechanism sibling of 5905CDEE (guard lock/Drop path) -- RELATES TO 5905CDEE; it was corroborated by the Correctness Reviewer P3 note that flagged TOCTOU specifically on clear_stale_readonly_lock during the 970AE45A/5D98DBCC adversarial review, whereas 5905CDEE (Security Reviewer P1) covers only the guard path. Needs its own spike/deliberation as a security-mechanism change (Constitution Principle III/IV). SCOPE GUARD: do NOT expand shipment 047-S / 048-S or the current dark activation scope to implement this -- deferred, separately-planned security bug. Source: PR #96 post-cap (cycle-3 hard-stop) residual conversion.
